text.p: On commodity markets on Friday evening, copper prices ended up $28 a tonne on news of a strike at Chile's Escondida copper mine and another LME stocks fall. Gold prices ended little changed, while oil prices jumped on short-covering ahead of the Northern Summer driving season.
Wheat prices also jumped on bad weather news in Europe and the United States.
The CRB Index closed up 2.03 at 247.34.
METALS - Copper prices were unable to penetrate the psychological $2,300 level during Friday afternoon LME trading, although the market still closed firmer.

Traders said copper received a partial boost from the start of the strike at Chile's Escondida - the world's largest copper mine. Although production is not expected to be affected, there was nevertheless some covering and buying after the news emerged, they said.

Other factors assisting copper's steadier trend were another LME warehouse stock fall, taking the total drawdown for the week to 7,200 tonnes, and a widening in the backwardation by some $15 to $45/50, basis cash/threes.
Prices peaked at $2,297 and then settled back on the kerb to $2,288 a tonne, still up $28 from Thursday.
Elsewhere in the base metals, copper's strength partially rubbed off on the other base metals, but there was little real volume in those markets.
Aluminium prices were constrained within a $10 band, which although steadier, was unexciting. Prices lost momentum towards the close, finishing at $1,554 a tonne, up just $4.
Nickel prices slipped back slightly from midsession highs, although the market remained firmer, building on the technical move above $7,300. Last trade was at $$7,345, up $75.
Zinc business remained dull throughout the afternoon, with the market content to stay corralled between $1,240 and $1,250, despite another stock fall. Last business was at $1,247, up just $4.
Alloy was steady throughout, with scattered business between $1,445 and $1,450. Three months closed at $1,445/50.

GOLD - COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended little changed Friday on low volumes, with gold prices still recovering from a test of the year's lows on Tuesday, and the platinum group metals (PGM's) still awaiting news on Russia's export intentions.
COMEX June gold closed down 90 cents at $343.40 an ounce, after trading a $343.00-345.20 range, inside Thursday's session range, after recovering from Wednesday's life-of-contract low at $339.50.

In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $341.10/60 compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $342.10 and the New York close Thursday around $342.30/80. But activity was light and the Jewish Passover holiday next week and the Islamic holiday of Id in the Middle East was slowing activity, traders said.

OIL - NYMEX crude ended with strong gains Friday on short covering ahead of the May crude contract expiry on Tuesday, pushing up prices of gasoline and heating oil in the rally. May crude ended 49 cents higher at $19.91 a barrel.
May heating oil ended 0.68 cent higher at 54.68 cents a gallon while May gasoline ended up 0.79 cent at 61.49 cents a gallon.

According to the most recent CFTC Futures Commitment of Traders report, speculators had set a large amount of short positions in crude, betting crude's price would fall. Indeed, since January, crude prices have dropped more than seven dollars a barrel on a surplus in domestic crude.
But refiner demand for crude picks up in May in order to make gasoline ahead of the summer driving season, pushing up crude prices and forcing traders to close their bet of a decline in crude.

GRAINS - New crop July CBOT wheat surged to a fresh 10-1/2 month high Friday and all contracts closed strongly higher on escalating concerns about crop losses in the U.S. and in the European Community, especially in France, traders said.

The July contract jumped to a session high of $4.47 per bushel which is a new 10-1/2-month high for that month. Traders cited persistent talk that the weekend freeze in the U.S. Great Plains may have damaged up to 200 million bushels of wheat.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to 13-1/2 cents higher with May up 11-3/4 at $4.37 and July up 13-1/2 at $4.44-1/2.
